title: Algebraic closure of the completion of a separably closed rank-one field
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed] with a nontrivial nonarchimedean real absolute value. Its metric completion $\widehat K$ is algebraically closed: every nonconstant polynomial over $\widehat K$ has a root. The inclusion $K\to\widehat K$ induces an isomorphism between the residue fields of $\{a\in K:|a|\leq1\}$ and $\{a\in\widehat K:|a|\leq1\}$, where the maximal ideals consist of the elements of absolute value less than one. In particular this common residue field is algebraically closed. Valuation rings have the meaning of [def-trf-valuation-ring].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13, first paragraph after the height-zero case: the completion and residue field of the separably closed height-one coarsening are algebraically closed.

proof.text: Put $F=\widehat K$. By [lem-sfb-normed-field-completion], $F$ is a complete normed field and $K\to F$ is an isometric field homomorphism. Identify $K$ with its image. Density is part of the meaning of metric completion: each $x\in F$ is a limit of a Cauchy sequence from $K$. The extended norm is nontrivial, since it preserves $|t|\ne0,1$ for a witness $t\in K$. It is nonarchimedean: for sequences $x_n\to x$, $y_n\to y$ from $K$, take limits in $|x_n+y_n|\le\max(|x_n|,|y_n|)$. Here continuity follows from $||u|-|v||\le|u-v|$ and $|(x_n+y_n)-(x+y)|\le|x_n-x|+|y_n-y|$.

proof.text: Fix a monic $f\in F[T]$ of degree $d\ge1$. By [lem-pc-algebraic-closure-exists-unique], choose an algebraic closure $L/F$; choose $a\in L$ with $f(a)=0$, using the root property in [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-trf-spectral-norm-algebraic-extension], equip $L$ with a multiplicative nonarchimedean real norm extending that of $F$. Its hypotheses hold: $F$ is complete and nontrivially nonarchimedean normed by step 1, and $L/F$ is algebraic. Neither $L$ nor $K$ is assumed complete.

source.place: Agent-supplied arbitrary-characteristic argument for the separably-closed upgrade listed in TODO (lines 23–30); context: Temkin, proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13. This proof replaces the characteristic-zero Krasner argument in Dense.lean, not a quotation of it.

proof.text: For every $\eta>0$, apply [lem-sfb-monic-dense-approximation] to $K\subset F$ to obtain monic $h\in K[T]$ of degree $d$ with $|h_i-f_i|<\eta$. Apply [lem-trf-separable-monic-approximation] over the original field $K$ to $h$ and $\eta$, obtaining monic separable $g\in K[T]$ of degree $d$ with $|g_i-h_i|<\eta$ for $i<d$. The ultrametric inequality gives $|g_i-f_i|<\eta$ for $i<d$; the leading coefficients agree and all higher coefficients vanish. The two approximation lemmas require no perfection or characteristic restriction. By [lem-trf-separable-polynomial-linear-factorization], $g(T)=\prod_{j=1}^d(T-b_j)$ with $b_j\in K$; there are exactly $d$ factors because degrees add for monic products over a field.

source.place: Agent-supplied arbitrary-characteristic argument for the separably-closed upgrade listed in TODO (lines 23–30); context: Temkin, proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13. This proof replaces the characteristic-zero Krasner argument in Dense.lean, not a quotation of it.

proof.text: Given $\epsilon>0$, let $M=\max(1,|a|)^{d-1}>0$ and choose the preceding $g$ with $\eta=\epsilon^d/(2M)$. Evaluating its coefficient difference from $f$ and using $f(a)=0$ gives $|g(a)|=|\sum_{i<d}(g_i-f_i)a^i|\le\max_{i<d}(|g_i-f_i||a|^i)<\eta M<\epsilon^d$. Multiplicativity and the displayed linear factorization give $|g(a)|=\prod_{j=1}^d|a-b_j|$. If all factors were at least $\epsilon$, this product would be at least $\epsilon^d$. Hence some $b\in K$ satisfies $|a-b|<\epsilon$. This is a finite-sum bound and a finite-product inequality; it uses no root-continuity or separability theorem beyond step 3.

source.place: Agent-supplied arbitrary-characteristic argument for the separably-closed upgrade listed in TODO (lines 23–30); context: Temkin, proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13. This proof replaces the characteristic-zero Krasner argument in Dense.lean, not a quotation of it.

proof.text: For $n\ge1$ choose $b_n\in K$ with $|a-b_n|<1/n$. Then $|b_n-b_m|\le\max(1/n,1/m)$, so $(b_n)$ is Cauchy in $F$ and has a limit $b\in F$ by step 1. The extended norm on $L$ restricts to that of $F$, and therefore $|a-b|\le\max(|a-b_n|,|b_n-b|)$ tends to zero. Thus $a=b$ in $L$, and injectivity of $F\hookrightarrow L$ gives $f(b)=0$ in $F$. Every nonconstant polynomial over $F$ becomes monic of the same positive degree after division by its nonzero leading coefficient, without changing its roots. Consequently $F$ is algebraically closed. No completeness of $L$ was used.

proof.text: For $E=K$ or $F$, put $\mathcal O_E=\{x:|x|\le1\}$ and $\mathfrak m_E=\{x:|x|<1\}$. The ultrametric and multiplicativity make $\mathcal O_E$ a subring and $\mathfrak m_E$ an ideal. An element of $\mathcal O_E$ outside $\mathfrak m_E$ has norm $1$, so its inverse also belongs to $\mathcal O_E$; elements of $\mathfrak m_E$ cannot be units. Thus $\mathfrak m_E$ is the unique maximal ideal. For $x\ne0$, either $|x|\le1$ or $|x^{-1}|<1$, giving the valuation-ring condition of [def-trf-valuation-ring]. The fraction field is $E$, since an element outside $\mathcal O_E$ is $1/x^{-1}$. These descriptions also show $\mathfrak m_F\cap\mathcal O_K=\mathfrak m_K$.

source.place: Agent-supplied arbitrary-characteristic argument for the separably-closed upgrade listed in TODO (lines 23–30); context: Temkin, proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13. This proof replaces the characteristic-zero Krasner argument in Dense.lean, not a quotation of it.

proof.text: The isometric inclusion therefore induces an injective ring map $\mathcal O_K/\mathfrak m_K\to\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak m_F$. It is surjective: for $x\in\mathcal O_F$, density supplies $b\in K$ with $|x-b|<1$. Then $|b|\le\max(|x|,|b-x|)\le1$, so $b\in\mathcal O_K$, and $x-b\in\mathfrak m_F$ means their residue classes agree. This proves the asserted canonical residue-field isomorphism.

source.place: Agent-supplied arbitrary-characteristic argument for the separably-closed upgrade listed in TODO (lines 23–30); context: Temkin, proof of Theorem 2.1.8, printed p. 13. This proof replaces the characteristic-zero Krasner argument in Dense.lean, not a quotation of it.

proof.text: To prove algebraic closedness of the residue field of $F$, take any monic polynomial $\bar P$ of positive degree $e$ over $\mathcal O_F/\mathfrak m_F$. Lift its lower coefficients to $c_i\in\mathcal O_F$ and set $P(T)=T^e+\sum_{i<e}c_iT^i$. Step 5 gives a root $z\in F$. If $|z|>1$, then $|z|^e>|c_i z^i|$ for every $i<e$, while $P(z)=0$ would imply $|z|^e=|\sum_{i<e}c_i z^i|\le\max_{i<e}|c_i z^i|$, a contradiction. Hence $z\in\mathcal O_F$; reduction gives $\bar P(\bar z)=0$. Normalize an arbitrary nonconstant residue polynomial by its leading coefficient. Thus every such polynomial has a root, and step 7 transfers this property to the common residue field.
